Acts in Motion

Every provision of an Act, zoomed out to fit one screen, played from 2007 to now. When an amendment takes effect, the parts it touches flash: green for new text, amber for text reworded in place, red for text removed (which then fades to a faint ghost). Switch the colour to Party to see which government was in office instead.

Moments to watch

How this is drawn

  • Each short line is about 60 characters of the Act, in document order, flowing down and across in columns like a printed page shrunk to fit. Headings are brighter. Indentation follows nesting: subsections, paragraphs, subparagraphs.
  • The layout includes every provision that ever existed in the period, so positions stay fixed. Space for text that hasn't been written yet is blank.
  • Rebuilt from legislation.docref.nz: the latest version's full text, then each version's changelog applied in reverse. Removed provisions are placed by their numbering and drawn at a typical length, since their text isn't in the changelogs. Under 1% of block IDs didn't line up during the rebuild.
  • Colour shows the government in office on the date a version took effect. That isn't always the government that passed the change, and the source doesn't record which party sponsored each bill.
  • The current National-led government is shown from 27 November 2023; this page does not reflect the result of the 2026 general election.
